publisher: Oxford University Press (for the Sleep Research Society and American Academy of Sleep Medicine)

referenceList.doiPolicy: Provide DOIs and URLs when appropriate; preprint citations are not permitted in the final published version and must be replaced with the peer-reviewed version of record before publication.

provenance.claim: mode: “consecutive numerical order by means of Arabic numerals placed in brackets,” placed “outside periods and commas and inside colons and semicolons.” Mapped to 'parenthetical-numeric' as the schema's closest fit for a numbered/bracketed system — the actual delimiter is square brackets, not round parentheses; see notes.
collapseRanges: “When three or more references are cited at one place in the manuscript, a hyphen should be used to join the first and last numbers of a series.”

authorTruncation: “Provide all authors' names when fewer than seven; when seven or more, list the first three and add et al.” Encoded as truncateWhenMoreThan: 6 (NOT 7) because the schema field means “the largest author count still printed in full”: the rule truncates AT seven authors, so six is the last untruncated count. keepFirstN: 3 per “list the first three”.

referenceList.entryTemplates.article: derived from the page's one worked example — “Lehert P, Falissard B. Multiple treatment comparison in narcolepsy: a network meta-analysis. Sleep. 2018; 41 (12). doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsy185.” — rather than an explicit generic pattern statement; SLEEP states it follows “the American Medical Association 10th Edition style guide” generally, so page ranges may also appear in some entries even though the one example shown omits them.

journalAbbreviation: the page says to “refer to 'List of Journals Indexed in Index Medicus'” (NLM/Index Medicus convention) — left null rather than mapped to the schema's 'iso4' option, since Index Medicus/NLM abbreviations are a distinct governing convention from ISO 4 even though outputs often coincide; forcing this into 'iso4' would misrepresent the actual stated policy.

formats/minDpi: “minimum of 300 dpi”; acceptable file types “.tif, .eps, or .pdf”; explicitly UNACCEPTABLE: “Figures embedded as images in a Word document or in PowerPoint slides.” “The Journal does not charge for color.”

Accessibility (not modeled as a schema field): “we require you to provide alt text (alternative text) descriptions for all images,” placed directly under the figure legend; must follow OUP's general contrast/text-accessibility guidance. No column-width, font-size, line-weight, or colorblind-palette rule is stated on this page — left null rather than assumed.

wordLimit.scope: total, plus as many references as needed; may include one figure or table; no section headings; max 3 authors

requiredSections.label: Title page (title, authors, affiliations, corresponding author)
Discussion (must include a limitations paragraph near the end)

provenance.claim: abstract/significance/keywords: structured abstract (“Study Objectives, Methods, Results, Conclusions and Keywords”) OR narrative single-paragraph option, “limited to 250 words”; Statement of Significance “limited to 120 words,” required for original articles and reviews only; “no fewer than three but no more than ten keywords.”

article-type limits: Perspectives “should not exceed 4,000 words in length and 50 references”; Research Letters “should have 1,200 words, 10 references, one figure or table, and no abstract”; Editorials “maximum length of 1,200 words plus as many references as needed... may include one figure or table,” no section headings, max 3 authors.

submissionFormat: “Manuscript should be provided in Microsoft Word”; “Lines should be double-spaced”; “Pages should be numbered”; explicitly “Do not number the lines” (opposite of Nature's line-number requirement — a checker must not assume all journals want line numbers). Initial submissions may be format-neutral (Word, RTF, or PDF).

runningHeadLimitChars left null despite a stated rule: the page says “Please do not include a running title” — a prohibition, not a character limit, so it does not map onto this numeric-limit field; recorded in notes instead.

notes: documentStyle is a DELTA over the always-on SUNA house style and states ONLY what the SLEEP author guidelines (https://academic.oup.com/sleep/pages/author-guidelines) actually say: figures are cited as 'Figure 1' (Arabic numerals, not 'Fig.'); figure captions go in a LIST placed after the manuscript text (figures are not embedded in the submitted Word file), encoded as figurePlacement: 'captions-list'; tables are placed after the References/Figure Captions List, encoded as tablePlacement: 'end'; and 'References (begins new page)', encoded as referencesStartNewPage: true. Everything the guidelines do not state (fonts, sizes, margins, spacing) inherits the SUNA default.

Directly fetched in full from academic.oup.com (not blocked, unlike the Elsevier/Cell/PNAS/HighWire domains researched for Neuron/PNAS/Brain Stimulation/JNeurosci in this batch) — high confidence, verbatim quotes throughout.

citations.mode is encoded as 'parenthetical-numeric' as the closest fit in the schema's three-way enum, but the ACTUAL delimiter SLEEP states is square brackets, not round parentheses — the schema has no distinct 'bracket-numeric' option, so this is a deliberate best-fit mapping (matching how the same tradeoff is handled for jne.json, whose reference style is also bracket-numeric).

SLEEP explicitly says 'Do not number the lines' — the opposite of Nature's/JNeurosci's line-number requirement. A compliance checker must treat lineNumbers as genuinely per-journal, not a universal default.

'No fewer than three but no more than ten keywords' and the 120-word Statement of Significance (distinct from, and following, the 250-word Abstract) are both required fields not modeled by the current PublisherProfile schema (no keywords or significance-statement slots exist) — recorded here in notes only, encoded structurally only as a requiredSections entry for the Statement of Significance.
Journal-specific style quirk recorded for completeness, not schema-relevant: do not use 'SD' as an abbreviation for sleep deprivation.
